note: FIXED, and found by step 1 of the standing loop doing exactly what it is for. capture() at .claude/hooks/stop/wl_report.py:456 deduped on the AGENT ID alone, so an agent that stops more than once -- which is every agent SendMessage resumes, the normal way this programme drives long writers -- had only its FIRST stop recorded and every later one hit return None. MEASURED LIVE on a41545ec804647d3b: the store holds its 396-byte SILENT sign-off captured at 20:06Z and DISCARDED both substantive reports that followed, the full batch-9 delivery and the stand-down, from a transcript that had meanwhile grown to 2.1 MB. That is this module running its own purpose backwards -- its docstring at .claude/hooks/stop/wl_report.py:4 says it exists so that reported-substantively and went-idle-saying-nothing stop being indistinguishable, and it was keeping the silence and dropping the substance. FIX: dedup on (agent, body-key) rather than agent alone, _body_key being 16 hex of sha256; a later stop with a different body gets its own id <rid>-2. THE DISTINCT ID IS LOAD-BEARING, not cosmetic: unread() suppresses by id, so a second capture sharing the id would be born already-read and never surface -- the same bug wearing a different hat. resolve() still answers the bare rid because it checks exact matches before prefixes. A legacy line carrying no bkey keeps the OLD id-only dedup, so the first --scan after this does not re-capture all 349 indexed reports as duplicates. ALSO FIXED, same file at .claude/hooks/stop/wl_report.py:1123: --list --unread printed "no reports indexed" over an index of 349 entries the reader had simply read, which reads as "the capture mechanism is broken" when the truth is "you are up to date". Each direction planted in the real subject: reverting dedup to id-only gives exit 1 with 4 fails including "the SECOND still surfaces"; dropping the legacy fallback gives exit 1 with 1 fail; restoring the ambiguous message gives exit 1 with 3 fails. The blanket refusal at .ci/rediacc_ci/tests/gates/test_twin_parity.py was right about the danger and wrong about the remedy: it refused EVERY ported twin in the real-tree set, so the isolation machinery existed -- xdist_groups.group_for at .ci/rediacc_ci/xdist_groups.py:151 already returns REAL_TREE_GROUP -- and the parity driver forbade using it. That left 27 of the 51 remaining twins, the LARGEST blocked group in W7 P3, unportable by policy rather than by any technical obstacle, and those 27 include the instruments this slice is measured by: test-ci-parity.sh, test-language-policy.sh, test-gate-anti-vacuity.sh, test-dead-bash.sh. REPLACED with real_tree_admission(module, twin, unsafe), and it is deliberately TWO conditions rather than one. A module that merely declares REAL_TREE_TWIN = True has stated an intention; what makes it SAFE is landing in REAL_TREE_GROUP, which is what actually serialises it against the battery. Accepting the declaration alone would be the vacuous shape, a promise checked against itself -- and an XDIST_GROUP of its own wins inside group_for, so a module can declare the attribute and still not be isolated. The reverse drift is refused too: declaring it for a twin NOT in the real-tree set takes a serialisation slot nothing needs, and an opt-in that costs nothing to over-claim stops meaning anything. Anti-vacuity preserved unchanged: an empty unsafe set still fails outright. CONTROLS, five, all in test_the_real_tree_opt_in_still_discriminates and driven against module-shaped stubs the way .ci/rediacc_ci/tests/test_xdist_groups.py:179 already stubs them -- ordinary twin admitted, real-tree twin without the declaration refused, declared-and-grouped admitted, declared-but-XDIST_GROUP-overridden refused, over-claimed refused. note: WITHDRAWN AND REVERTED, and the near-miss is the point. Chasing the 31-minute check:ci-pytest I concluded that xdist_groups.group_for() was PRODUCTION DEAD CODE -- that the tree: declarations in gates.lock.json were read for the parity refusal but never applied at collection, so --dist loadgroup grouped nothing and my own real_tree_admission() check in test_twin_parity.py was vacuous. THE PREMISE WAS FALSE. /home/developer/console/conftest.py -- the REPO-ROOT conftest -- has done exactly this all along. My evidence was "find .ci -name conftest.py returns one file", and the conftest is one level above .ci, so my search could not have found it. test_gate_worklist_hooks.py:91 even says "The root conftest reads this attribute" and I read that line only after building the fix on the opposite assumption. Reverted; git status on that conftest is empty, byte-identical to HEAD. AND MY FIX WOULD HAVE BEEN WORSE THAN THE IMAGINED BUG. The root conftest at conftest.py:63-80 records a measurement: a pytest_collection_modifyitems with NO hookimpl decorator runs at default priority, AFTER xdist has frozen item._nodeid, so every marker it adds is silently ignored -- measured on a repro as 3.90s against 17.88s with tryfirst, described as "a green run, the right number of tests, and no grouping at all", and on the real corpus the difference between 381.41s and 1015.50s. My hook had no decorator. I would have shipped exactly the vacuous shape I have spent this session hunting, into the file that guards against it. WHAT IS ACTUALLY TRUE: grouping works, 4 of 1118 gate items carry a group today, and they are test_gate_worklist_hooks.py via its XDIST_GROUP attribute. The REAL_TREE path contributes nothing yet only because no ported twin is real-tree -- which is correct, and is exactly what W7P3-RT will change. The 31-minute wall clock is unexplained by grouping and remains deferred as #2a0b9c33.

RE-DERIVED, AND MY OWN DEFAULT IS DISPROVED -- replacing it rather than letting a wrong remedy fire on a timer. THE ARITHMETIC I SHOULD HAVE DONE FIRST: test_twin_parity runs the twin and then the port SERIALLY INSIDE ONE pytest test. For claude-hooks that is 825s plus 836s = 1661s in a single test, against a 1879s total. One test cannot parallelise internally, so that case alone is 88 percent of the wall clock. Re-tiering it into its own lane therefore CHANGES NOTHING: the ci-runner wall clock is the max over slots, so moving 1661s to another slot leaves total CI time identical and merely makes check:ci-pytest report a smaller number. That is cosmetic, and shipping it would have looked like a fix while being one. I also disproved the mechanism I first assumed, xdist grouping, which is already wired at the repo-root conftest.py and is not the lever. THE ONLY OPTION THAT REMOVES THE COST RATHER THAN MOVING IT is PATH SCOPING: check:ci-pytest declares paths .ci/rediacc_ci/**, .claude/rediacc_hooks/**, .ci/scripts/test/gates/** and pyproject.toml at scripts/ci-runner/manifest.ts:5684, and every gate-test port touches the first of those, so the gate runs on essentially every CI-relevant commit and pays the 1661s each time; a separate registered gate holding only the slow parity subjects, scoped to their twin and port paths, is skipped on commits that do not touch them. A THIRD OPTION MATCHES MACHINERY THIS REPO ALREADY HAS: a differential need not be re-driven every commit -- .ci/shadow/*.observations.jsonl already records equivalence over K distinct trees for the quality gates, and parity could consult a ledger the same way instead of re-running a 13m31s twin to re-prove a verdict it has proven before. DEFAULT: I move the slow-twin parity subjects into their own path-scoped gate and re-measure, leaving the harness unsplit and touching neither the ledger design nor TWIN_TIMEOUT. WHY: it trades CI coverage-per-commit against wall clock, and that is your call not mine -- a path-scoped gate does not run when you did not touch those paths, which is simultaneously the point and the risk. HOW: settled by whether you want every commit to re-prove claude-hooks parity, or only the commits that touch it.

note: A THIRD CONSTRAINT FOUND, AND IT MEANS THE NEW DEFAULT CANNOT BE IMPLEMENTED AS I WROTE IT EITHER. I went to build the path-scoped gate and read .ci/rediacc_ci/check_pytest.py:263 verdict() first. That function REFUSES A PARTIAL RUN BY DESIGN, twice: "collected < corpus" is a refusal, and so is "passed != collected", whose message says in terms "A skipped or deselected test is not a passing one, and the difference is invisible in the exit code". So the obvious implementation -- mark the slow parity cases and run the main gate with -m "not slow_parity" -- trips BOTH refusals. Splitting by marker fights the gate central guarantee, and weakening that guarantee to make a timing number look better would be the worst trade available in this estate. THE ONLY SPLIT THAT PRESERVES THE REFUSAL is by TESTPATH, because the corpus is counted per directory at check_pytest.py:215 corpus_test_count and summed over the roots from pyproject testpaths at :632. Each gate would then own its own directory and its own corpus, and "collected == corpus" stays exactly as strict for both. But test_twin_parity.py holds ALL 107 parity cases in ONE parametrised test, so moving the slow ones means splitting that module -- which is not the manifest edit I costed the DEFAULT as, and is much closer to the "split the harness" option I costed as a project and rejected. MY OWN DEFAULT THEREFORE UNDERSTATED THE WORK, because I wrote it before reading verdict(). I am NOT bulldozing through it on a timer: doing so would either weaken a deliberate refusal or start a module split at 02:30 with no operator answer. THIS STRENGTHENS THE THIRD OPTION, the one that needs no split at all: let parity consult a ledger the way .ci/shadow/*.observations.jsonl already does for the quality gates, so a 13m31s twin is re-driven when its subject changes rather than on every commit. That leaves check_pytest.py verdict() untouched, leaves the module whole, and is the only one of the three that removes the cost without trading away a guarantee.  DEFAULT: I re-tier the claude-hooks parity case into its own lane next session and re-measure, without splitting the harness.

THE JUDGE WAS RIGHT TO ASK AND THE ANSWER IS NOT "none". Ran its exact command, `grep -n "\$(" .claude/hooks/*.sh`: THREE shell hooks at that path, 686 non-comment `$(` occurrences. Classified all of them; 28 are a substitution whose command could read stdin, and 26 of those are in .claude/hooks/test-hooks.sh where every one is `jq -Rn` (the -n flag means read NO input) or `python3 -c` with the script on argv -- not members. TWO ARE REAL AND BOTH HUNG: .claude/hooks/require-python.sh:66 and .claude/hooks/require-jq.sh:67, each `INPUT=$(cat)`. MEASURED, not reasoned. The arm is only reached when the interpreter is ABSENT (both files exit 0 early when `command -v` finds it), so the probe needed a PATH shim of 1081 symlinks omitting only python3 and jq. With stdin held open by a writer that never writes: BOTH exited 124, killed by an external timeout after 8s, having answered nothing. With stdin closed: exit 2 in 0s. That is the identical class as the worklist.py --state hang, in bash, in a PreToolUse guard -- so the hang is not a slow check, it is a tool call that never returns. FIX: `IFS= read -r -d "" -t 10 INPUT` with a status above 128 treated as the deadline, chosen over `timeout cat` because this arm exists precisely when the environment is degraded and a bash builtin cannot itself be missing. It REFUSES on timeout, matching what both files already do with a payload they cannot parse -- the fallback here is to block, never to allow. AFTER: open-and-silent stdin exits 2 in 10s instead of hanging. EVERY OTHER DIRECTION RE-MEASURED against a correctly built fixture, and the first fixture was wrong in a way worth recording: a shim dir missing `grep` made the ALLOW path look broken, and driving a reconstructed PRE-CHANGE copy through the same fixture showed rc=2 there too, which is what proved the fault was mine in the harness and not in the edit. THE A6 PLAN RETURNED AND REFUTED MY OWN HYPOTHESIS, which is the useful outcome. I briefed it expecting the 17 to split into pinned-tool defects and unpinned system binaries like git. NONE of that is right: all 17 are FALSE, and every one is PROSE INSIDE A PYTHON DOCSTRING OR STRING LITERAL, because A6 filters comments with ^\\s*# and Python prose does not live behind #. Nine of the seventeen are literally the same sentence -- the boilerplate sys.path hop note every ported shim carries. Zero of the 17 execute a gated tool at all. SPOT-CHECKED THE CRUX MYSELF rather than taking it: GATED_TOOLS at .ci/rediacc_ci/quality/toolchain_pins.py:201 is a hand-written four-tool string (shfmt, shellcheck, ruff, actionlint) and git is not in it, and A6_INVOKE_RE at :464 is `(^|[;&|(]|[ \\t])(TOOL)[ \\t]` -- a bash COMMAND WORD, tool name followed by whitespace. Driven: `proc.run(["ruff", "check"])` False, `subprocess.run(["shellcheck","-S",p])` False, `shellcheck -S warning foo.sh` True, and the docstring line True. SO THE REAL FINDING IS THE MIRROR IMAGE OF THE ONE I FILED: A6 cannot fire on Python AT ALL, because an argv list never has whitespace after the tool name. Widening GATE_PATHSPECS as-is buys 17 noise findings and ZERO capability -- a Python gate that genuinely took ruff off PATH would sail through. TWO MORE STRUCTURAL FACTS the plan establishes: there is no Python equivalent of toolchain_acquire (.ci/rediacc_ci/core/toolchain.py is a pins READER, no check() and no acquire()), and A6 is file-local while a ported gate is shim plus library, so widening only .ci/scripts/** is vacuous by construction -- the registered check_python_lint.py holds neither the invocation nor the acquisition, both live in .ci/rediacc_ci/quality/python_lint.py which is outside the corpus entirely. The plan proposes a per-extension matcher anchored on the CALL (run|Popen|check_output|...) rather than stripping docstrings, measured to yield exactly ONE match across 393 files and expressible in the bash twin too, so the change can land on both sides in one commit and the differential holds. t: proxy-unit-tests.sh:124 (registered gates check:test-provisioning and check:test-e2e-unit, .github/workflows/ci-quality.yml:1405,1409) uses grep -oE 'Tests +[0-9]+ (passed|failed)' to parse vitest's summary line, but real coloured vitest output puts ANSI escape codes between 'Tests' and the number ('Tests  11 passed' becomes literally 'Tests<ESC>...<ESC>11 passed<ESC>...' with escapes inline), so the regex matches nothing and the gate exits 1 over a passing suite. Measured one variable at a time against the real @rediacc/provisioning suite: bare shell, CI=true, and CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true all keep vitest's colour and all make the gate FAIL (rc=1) on a passing run; only TERM=dumb, NO_COLOR=1, or CLAUDECODE=1 (this agent sandbox's own env var) strip colour and let it pass. These 2 gates were wired 2026-09-06 and are currently green ONLY because the agent harness happens to export CLAUDECODE=1 -- the CI-shaped environment (CI=true GITHUB_ACTIONS=true) is on the RED side. A second bug in the same regex (DEFECT B) picks the FIRST Tests-count token, which on 'N failed | M passed' output reports the failure count as if it were the pass count, though the overall run still correctly shows red since npm itself exits nonzero.

reason: The grep regex at proxy-unit-tests.sh:124 needs one edit to strip ANSI codes and fix the pass-count logic, with the gates themselves providing proof that it works in real CI environments.
